Why Christian children's books belong at home

Christian children's books give families an easy way to talk about God at the kitchen table, in the car and at bedtime. That is where much of a child's faith is shaped.

Church leaders agree. In a Barna Group study done with Cardus, nearly all Protestant pastors and Catholic priests ranked parents first, ahead of the church, as responsible for children's faith formation. In an earlier Barna survey, most parents of children under 13 said that job was theirs, too.

Research from the Pew Research Center points the same way. A religious upbringing often leads to a religious adulthood, though not always. Adults who grew up in homes where faith was talked about a lot were more likely to keep their parents' faith than adults whose parents rarely discussed it.

A book makes those talks easier. You do not have to plan a lesson. You read the story, and the questions come on their own.

What you will find on this shelf

The names of God. A group of books, each built around one name of God, such as Jehovah Jireh: My Provider!, Jehovah Rapha: My Healer!, Jehovah Shalom: My Peace!, El Shaddai: All-Sufficient! and Elohim The Creator.

Prayer and thanks. Titles such as Talia's Starry Prayer, Grandma Sara's Prayer Power, Sammy's Thankful Tree and The Thankful Tractor.

Verses on the cover. Seeking First: Matthew 6:33, We Love Because He First Loved Us: 1 John 4:19 and The Prayer of Salvation: Romans 10:9-10 each name a Bible passage in the title.

Faith stories with fun characters. Franklin's Leap of Faith, Ernie the Eraser's Gift of Grace, Colin the Compass: God's Guide and Arthur the Anchor Holds Fast, among many more.

Bible stories. Noah's Ark, Jonah and the Big Fish, David and Goliath and others have their own page: Bible story books for kids.

Tips for reading faith books together

  • Read it twiceNAEYC, the national early childhood group, tells families to reread children's favorites. A second reading is when kids start asking questions.
  • Find the verseIf a book names a verse, open your Bible and read it together. Let your child put a finger on the words.
  • Pray about the storyEnd with a one-line prayer about what you read: "Thank you, God, for taking care of us like you did for Noah."
  • Bring in grandparentsGrandparents can read over a video call or keep a few books at their house for visits.

"And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up."

Deuteronomy 6:7 (KJV)

Questions parents ask

What are good Christian books for 2 and 3 year olds?

Look for short books with one simple idea, such as God made the world, God loves you, or saying thank you. Read them often. Short titles like My Heart Is Happy: A Little Book of God's Blessings fit this kind of reading.

What Christian books work for 6, 7 and 8 year olds?

At this age many children can read some words themselves. Books built around one name of God or one Bible verse give them something to look up and talk about. The Jehovah Jireh, Jehovah Rapha and El Shaddai books are examples.

Are there Christian books for 2nd graders that teach a Bible verse?

Some titles here name a verse right on the cover, such as Seeking First: Matthew 6:33 and The Prayer of Salvation: Romans 10:9-10. Read the verse in your Bible together after the story.

Which Bible translation do these pages quote?

This site quotes only the King James Version, word for word. Each book's own Amazon page is the place to check what a book uses.
